title: AB 2047 Loses Its Teeth, INDX Gen 2 Ships & Sovol's $3.2M Finish
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: AB 2047: Gutted Before the Final Vote
topics.description: The August 17 amendments hollowed the bill out — and the session ends Monday

slides.heading: AB 2047: Quietly Gutted Before the Final Vote
slides.body: Last week the printer-blocking bill was headed to the Senate floor with its mandate intact. Not anymore. Amendments filed August 17 hollowed out the enforcement chain, and on August 18 the amended bill was ordered to third reading. The floor vote deadline is Monday, August 31 — this ends within days.
bullets: The DOJ-standards → manufacturer-attestations → approved-printer-list chain is gone from the bill
The Dec 1, 2029 sales restriction now hangs on a standards body that hasn't written the standard
Ordered to third reading Aug 18 — the full Senate is the next and final stop before concurrence
Same QR as the last three weeks — the tracker updates the moment the floor votes

slides.heading: The ASTM Off-Ramp: A Mandate Becomes a Tripwire
slides.body: The amended bill hands the hard part to ASTM International, the industry standards body — and builds in its own exit.
bullets: From July 1, 2027: California DOJ checks quarterly whether ASTM has published a firearm-blocking standard for 3D printers
If ASTM publishes one, the state gets 24 months to issue guidance based on it
If ASTM publishes nothing by July 1, 2029, the department 'shall not be required to make any further determinations' — it just stops
No ASTM standard exists today, and ASTM is under no obligation to write one

slides.heading: What Happens by Monday
slides.body: Report it straight: the bill is still alive and still advancing — it's just carrying far less than it did two weeks ago.
bullets: Senate floor vote by Aug 31 (session end), then Assembly concurrence in the amendments, then Newsom's desk
No floor date was set as of Thursday — it could happen while we're meeting
The opposition coalition (Průša, VORON, Make, Joel Telling, EFF) hasn't stood down — a weakened bill still normalizes the idea
Copycats to watch either way: Washington HB 2320/2321, New York (Hochul)

topics.title: INDX Gen 2: Kits Ship, Full Printers On Sale
topics.description: The toolchanger saga hits its biggest week since the Founders Edition

slides.heading: INDX Gen 2: Kits Are Shipping, Full Printers On Sale
slides.body: August 20: Prusa started shipping the first batch of INDX conversion kits and opened orders for a complete CORE One+ (Gen 2) with Bondtech INDX — the first time you can buy the toolchanger machine whole instead of converting.
bullets: Complete printer options: assembled or kit, 4-tool or 8-tool — assembled runs $1,999 (4-tool) / $2,249 (8-tool)
Conversion kits cover both the CORE One+ and the Gen 2
Today (Aug 27): the bigger CORE One L+ joined — conversion kits and assembled L+ INDX printers both open for orders
Prusa notes the Founders Edition hardware isn't identical to this standard edition — refinements landed in between

slides.heading: Still Owed From the Saga
bullets: The promised 'State of INDX' blog post still hasn't appeared — shipping apparently outran the write-up
PrusaSlicer 3.0 alpha is still 'weeks away' — no release this week from Prusa, Orca, or Bambu Studio
Founders Edition owners: watch for the firmware updates that carry the Gen 2 refinements back

topics.title: Sovol M1D: Funded at $3.19M
topics.description: The campaign closed meetup morning — after a final-week slide

slides.heading: Sovol M1D: Funded at $3.19M — After a Final-Week Slide
slides.body: The IDEX-toolchanger Kickstarter closed this morning at 10AM: $3,187,254 from 2,027 backers, roughly 16x its goal. The oddity is the direction it closed in — a week ago it stood at $3.44M and 2,176 backers.
bullets: Final week net change: about −$253k in pledges and −149 backers — people pulled out at the wire
Late pledges are open if you missed the campaign
We backed two — delivery expected around November
Standing Kickstarter caveat: it's a pledge, not a purchase — November is a promise, not a ship date

topics.title: Print Orientation: You Asked
topics.description: Members asked how to orient prints for strength and detail — here's the map

slides.heading: Print Orientation 101: Strength Is Directional
slides.body: Members asked about this last week, so let's cover the fundamentals. A print isn't equally strong in every direction — the layer seams are the weak points, and orientation decides whether your load runs along the plastic or pries the seams apart.
bullets: Flat in X/Y: force runs along the layers — the strong direction
Upright in Z: force pulls layer seams apart — the weak direction, parts snap at a seam
Orientation also sets surface detail: the walls facing up/out print cleaner than surfaces fighting the layer stack

slides.heading: The Classic Explainer
slides.body: Maker's Muse's orientation walkthrough is a decade old and still the clearest starting point — the physics hasn't changed.

slides.heading: The 45° Trick
slides.body: CNC Kitchen tested tilting parts 45° instead of printing them flat or upright: no load direction hits the seams square-on, so you trade a little peak strength for decent strength in more directions.

topics.title: Robotics Corner: A Robot Dog on Four Servos
topics.description: Petoi's Quaddle walks on half the usual hardware — plus builds you can start tonight

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: A Robot Dog That Walks on Four Servos
slides.body: Petoi's Quaddle is a mini desk robot dog that walks, glides sideways, and spins in place on just 4 servos — most quadrupeds need 8 to 12. It runs on OpenCat (yes, the dog runs on OpenCat — that's the name of Petoi's open-source quadruped framework), and you can dress it up with your own printed shells and LEGO-compatible mounts.
bullets: Programming ladder: drag-and-drop blocks → Python → C++ → ROS — same framework as their Bittle robot dog
Kickstarter hasn't launched yet — August signup list now, early-bird tiers listed at $99 / $139 / $179
Honest print caveat: shells and mounts are printable, but the load-critical joints stay injection-molded
Usual Kickstarter rules apply — nothing is real until it ships

slides.heading: Don't Want to Wait? Build One Tonight
slides.body: Max asked the better question: what can members actually print and build right now? These three are fully published — files, firmware, and build docs are up today.
bullets: Open Duck Mini — the ~$400 printable walking duck we covered in W27; files and RL walking policies on GitHub
TOPS — Aaed Musa's open-source printed quadruped ('SPOT' backwards): full CAD, code, and build video
Berkeley Humanoid Lite — an open-source 3D-printed HUMANOID with printable cycloidal gearboxes, for the ambitious

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: soiboi's Air-Powered Display
topics.description: A 64-pixel display that runs on vacuum instead of electricity

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: soiboi's Air-Powered Display
slides.body: This week's spotlight is soiboi soft, who built a 64-pixel dot display that runs entirely on air — no electronics in the display at all. It's 3D-printed fluidic logic: channels and valves printed into rigid plates with a silicone membrane in between.

slides.heading: How You Compute With Air
bullets: The logic levels are pressures: near-vacuum is a 1, atmospheric pressure is a 0
The clever part is multiplexing — one valve per row and one per column drives all 64 pixels, instead of one valve per pixel
An earlier build strung vacuum-powered 'transistors' into pneumatic RAM — a clock display that remembers its digits with zero electricity
Print the plates, add a silicone sheet and a vacuum source — the whole logic family is printable

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Maintenance 101 — your printer wants ten minutes a month

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Clean Your Lead Screws (Maintenance 101)
slides.body: Those greased vertical screws that move your Z axis are dust magnets — and old grease plus dust turns into grinding paste that shows up as banding and Z artifacts in your prints. LayerLab's fix takes ten minutes: wipe the old grease off with a rag and isopropyl, then re-apply a thin coat of fresh grease.

slides.heading: The Rest of the Ten-Minute Checklist
bullets: Wipe the build plate with dish soap and water — finger oils are the top cause of adhesion loss (IPA between washes)
Check belt tension — loose belts read as layer shifts and ringing
Clear filament dust out of the extruder drive gears
Vacuum the fans and electronics bay — dust is insulation your stepper drivers don't want
Keep filament dry — wet filament wastes every other minute you spent on this list
